diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (WHO 2022 / ICC). Left cervical level IV excisional biopsy (collected 2026-09-09, final 2026-09-11, FISH addendum 2026-09-16). Non-germinal-center B-cell phenotype by Hans algorithm (CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1/IRF4+ in ~70%). Double-expressor by IHC (MYC ~50%, BCL2 ~80%). Ki-67 ~85%. CD5-, CD30-, cyclin D1-, EBER-, lambda-restricted. No MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement by FISH, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement (double/triple-hit). Not primary mediastinal (CD30-, retroperitoneal disease, no PMBCL profile), not Burkitt (CD10-, no MYC rearrangement), not blastoid mantle cell (CD5-, cyclin D1-). Bone marrow uninvolved (aspirate and biopsy collected 2026-09-10).
stage: Lugano 2014 / Ann Arbor stage III, B (fever 38.1-38.5 C and drenching night sweats), with bulky disease (retroperitoneal mass 11.0 x 8.1 cm, above the 10 cm threshold). Nodal disease above the diaphragm: left cervical levels III-IV, right paratracheal and subcarinal. Nodal disease below the diaphragm: left para-aortic/aortocaval retroperitoneal mass, plus spleen 14.2 cm with at least four FDG-avid lesions. Lugano counts the spleen as a nodal site, so splenic involvement does not by itself make stage IV. There is no other extranodal disease and the marrow is negative. Weight loss from 86 to 78.4 kg is about 9%, under the 10% criterion, so B status rests on fever and night sweats. If the splenic lesions were scored as extranodal, the stage would be IV. That would not change treatment.
biology: Non-GCB phenotype with double-expressor features (MYC protein ~50% and BCL2 protein ~80%) and no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement by FISH. Non-GCB and double-expressor status are adverse prognostic markers under R-CHOP-type therapy, but without rearrangement they do not by themselves justify a different regimen outside a trial. The karyotype report was requested on 2026-09-11 and is not in the chart, so complex karyotype and TP53 status are unknown. TP53 status is prognostic and should be documented. Cell-of-origin gene expression profiling would not change the first-line decision and is not needed.
prognosis: Curable intent. IPI is 3 (age over 60, LDH above ULN, stage III), which is high-intermediate. aaIPI is 3 (high). NCCN-IPI is about 5 (high-intermediate: age 61-75 = 2, LDH above 3x ULN = 2, stage III = 1). LDH is 3.0x ULN on 9/3 and 3.3x ULN on 9/16, so the LDH point is not borderline. B symptoms, bulk, non-GCB and double-expressor status all weigh against him. Favorable features are ECOG 1, normal renal and hepatic function, normal LVEF, and no prior therapy. With standard first-line immunochemotherapy I would expect roughly 60-70% long-term remission. Relapse risk is about one in three, and is probably higher given the double-expressor phenotype. In POLARIX (IPI 2-5), 2-year PFS was about 77% with pola-R-CHP versus about 70% with R-CHOP. Subgroup data for double-expressor disease are limited, so these figures are population estimates, not individual predictions.
first_line_treatment: Pola-R-CHP (polatuzumab vedotin, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone) every 21 days for 6 cycles, with primary G-CSF prophylaxis, aiming for C1 within about 2 weeks of tumor board. Start only after the HBV DNA result is back and entecavir is started, the uric acid/TLS plan is in place, and the current CBC and CMP are reviewed. Doses on BSA 1.97 m2 and weight 78.4 kg (verify against day-of-treatment weight): rituximab 375 mg/m2 (about 740 mg) D1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 (about 1480 mg) D1; doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 (about 99 mg) D1, cumulative 300 mg/m2 over 6 cycles, well under the 450 mg/m2 limit with LVEF 58%; polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg (about 140 mg) D1; prednisone 100 mg D1-5. No vincristine: polatuzumab replaces it, which removes the neuropathy risk, and his baseline neurologic exam is normal. Reasons: he has IPI 2-5 with bulky stage III disease and is fit for full-dose therapy, and POLARIX showed a PFS benefit over R-CHOP. DA-EPOCH-R is reserved for confirmed MYC plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 double- or triple-hit disease, which is not present. Without rearrangement there is no randomized evidence it is superior, it is more toxic, and its 96-hour ambulatory pump each cycle conflicts with his work and travel. R-CHOP-21 is an acceptable fallback if polatuzumab cannot be obtained. I would not add ibrutinib, lenalidomide or bortezomib outside a trial. A central venous port is recommended because doxorubicin is a vesicant. Refer for trial screening in parallel, but do not delay C1 for it.
cns_risk: CNS-IPI is intermediate, about 2-3 depending on whether splenic involvement counts as an extranodal site. Age over 60, stage III and elevated LDH each score. Kidney and adrenal disease is absent. Testicular, paranasal sinus and epidural disease are absent, and the marrow is negative. He has no CNS symptoms and a normal neuro exam. Decision: no CNS-directed prophylaxis (intrathecal or high-dose methotrexate), and no baseline lumbar puncture or brain MRI unless neurologic symptoms appear. Double-expressor status alone is not an indication. Revisit if the karyotype shows MYC plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, which would change the regimen and the CNS discussion, or if kidney, adrenal, testicular or sinus involvement is found on restaging.
response_assessment: Baseline FDG PET-CT on 2026-09-05 is the reference. Every involved site is Deauville 5 (SUVmax 13.9-22.4 against liver SUVmax 2.6). Target lesions: retroperitoneal mass 11.0 x 8.1 cm (SUVmax 22.4), left cervical node 3.1 x 2.4 cm, right paratracheal 2.6 cm, subcarinal 2.2 cm, and splenic lesions up to 2.4 cm. Interim PET-CT after C2 for prognosis and to plan consolidation RT. A Deauville 4-5 result at interim does not change the standard regimen; I would continue and discuss trials. End-of-treatment PET-CT 4-6 weeks after C6 (Lugano). Complete metabolic response is Deauville 1-3 with no new lesions. Deauville 4-5 at the retroperitoneal site: consolidation RT to about 30-36 Gy. If the residual site is Deauville 4-5 and RT is not possible, biopsy before any change in therapy. Progressive disease: biopsy and salvage planning. Clinically, fevers and night sweats should resolve by C2-C3. Persistent fever beyond C1 needs an infection workup, and a rising LDH needs evaluation for progression. Use the same modality for comparison; outside CT of 2026-08-18 is for reference only.
pretreatment_workup: Repeat CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid, phosphate, magnesium and calcium now (last full set 9/16) and within 72 hours before C1. Quantitative HBV DNA now. HBsAg-negative with anti-HBc and anti-HBs positive means resolved or vaccinated exposure, and rituximab makes this high risk for reactivation. Start entecavir 0.5 mg daily before C1, continuing at least 12 months after the last rituximab (many centers use 18 months); do not delay C1 for the DNA result, but start entecavir now. Document the karyotype report, which was requested and is not in the chart. Document TP53 status (IHC, sequencing, or 17p FISH). Neither result should delay C1 unless the karyotype shows a double-hit. Also order: baseline ECG (QTc, antiemetic planning); quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG) before rituximab; HbA1c or glucose baseline for the steroid pulses; repeat TSH; ferritin and iron studies given the anemia; and G6PD only if rasburicase becomes necessary. Port placement. Echocardiogram already done (LVEF 58%, GLS -20%); repeat only for new symptoms. Infection: UA and blood cultures negative in August. Repeat cultures and chest X-ray if fever of 38.0 C or higher at a visit. Screen for latent TB per institutional policy. Vaccines: inactivated influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal conjugate and recombinant zoster, ideally at least 2 weeks before C1. No live vaccines. Offer fertility counseling. No brain MRI, lumbar puncture or repeat marrow is needed.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis: uric acid rose from 6.8 to 7.1 with LDH above 3x ULN and an 11 cm mass, so TLS risk is intermediate to high. Start allopurinol 300 mg daily now. Hydrate 2-3 L/day around C1 and check potassium, phosphate, creatinine and uric acid daily for the first 3 days. Use rasburicase only if uric acid keeps rising on allopurinol or renal function falls (check G6PD first). Growth factor: pegfilgrastim or biosimilar on D4 of every cycle as primary prophylaxis, because R-CHOP-type febrile neutropenia risk is about 20% and he has age over 60, advanced stage and B symptoms. Antiemetics: moderate emetic risk (doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide under 1500 mg/m2), so NK1 antagonist plus 5-HT3 antagonist, with dexamethasone per protocol. PJP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX (SS daily or DS three times weekly) during prednisone cycles is reasonable; institutional practice varies. Antiviral HSV/VZV prophylaxis is not routinely needed. Fever: check temperature before taking acetaminophen. Call for 38.0 C or higher and follow the febrile neutropenia pathway. Cap acetaminophen at 3 g/day and avoid NSAIDs because of platelets, the renal mass and possible rituximab effects. Anemia: Hb 10.8, normocytic, anemia of inflammation; transfuse for Hb below 7 or symptoms; no ESA. Hypothyroidism: continue levothyroxine; PPI can reduce absorption, so recheck TSH in 6-8 weeks. Steroids: glucose 104; monitor during prednisone. Retroperitoneal mass with left flank ache: monitor creatinine each visit; urgent imaging for flank pain, falling urine output or rising creatinine. Spleen 14.2 cm: avoid contact sports and heavy lifting; report left upper quadrant or shoulder-tip pain urgently. Cardiac: LVEF 58%; continue atorvastatin; monitor BP. Neuropathy: check each visit (polatuzumab). Rituximab premedication and first-infusion titration. Alopecia: expected with doxorubicin; scalp cooling may give partial protection with anthracyclines, and wig referral. Nutrition: about 9% weight loss; dietitian referral and weight each visit. Social work and psycho-oncology support for him and his wife. Advise minimal alcohol during treatment, especially with acetaminophen and during neutropenia. Interaction check before any azole antifungal (atorvastatin myopathy and future vincristine use).
fitness_and_goals: He is fit for full-dose curative therapy. He is 62, ECOG 1 (tires by mid-afternoon but fully independent), with eGFR 96, normal bilirubin and transaminases, LVEF 58%, controlled hypothyroidism, no prior cancer and no prior chemotherapy or radiation. GERD, hyperlipidemia and resolved HBV are management issues, not barriers. His goals are cure and being well for his daughter's wedding in May 2027. Timeline: six cycles of 21 days is about 18 weeks. If C1 starts by early November 2026, C6 finishes around end of February to March 2027, end-of-treatment PET follows in about April, and any consolidation RT can finish before May. Each week of delay moves the end of therapy toward the wedding, so I would tell him that. Work: he can continue part-time from home through treatment, with fatigue expected around days 3-10 of each cycle. Job-site travel about once a month is acceptable with conditions. Avoid travel during the expected nadir (roughly days 7-14 of each cycle). Stay within reach of the cancer center for the first cycle, carry a chemotherapy alert card, and do not travel while febrile or unwell. Re-review after C1 counts and tolerance. Hair loss: alopecia is expected with doxorubicin; scalp cooling is an option with partial effect. Fertility: offer discussion, though at 62 it is not usually the main concern. Driving is acceptable if he is not sedated.
